entry.title: Genomic and epidemiological analysis of *Vibrio parahaemolyticus* O10:K4, a newly emerging serotype in China

link.title: Genomic and epidemiological analysis of *Vibrio parahaemolyticus* O10:K4, a newly emerging serotype in China

entry.content:
The Quick Summary

A tiny germ called Vibrio parahaemolyticus often makes people sick from eating seafood. A new type of this germ, called O10:K4, has quickly become a big problem in China since around 2020. Scientists are studying these germs from sick people to understand how they spread and cause illness.

Original Abstract

Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a leading cause of seafood-associated bacterial gastroenteritis, which poses increasing public health challenges worldwide. Since its emergence in approximately 2020, VP O10:K4 has rapidly become the dominant cause of gastroenteritis in China. Serotyping classification against 76 clinical isolates from Shandong indicated that O10:K4 reached a detection rate of approximately 90% by 2023. entry.title: A CRISPR/*Cas12a*-MXene Nanozyme Platform for Universal Detection of Trace DNA

link.title: A CRISPR/*Cas12a*-MXene Nanozyme Platform for Universal Detection of Trace DNA

entry.content:
The Quick Summary

Scientists have created a new, easy-to-use tool to find tiny pieces of DNA without needing big laboratory machines. This tool uses a special system called CRISPR/Cas12a combined with a material called MXene to spot the DNA. When the tool finds the specific DNA it’s looking for, it creates a visible color change, making it simple to detect even very small amounts.

Original Abstract

The instrument-free detection of specific DNA sequences is critical for point-of-care diagnostics yet remains challenging. To address this, we developed a universal colorimetric biosensing platform integrating the CRISPR/Cas12a system with MXene nanozymes. Target recognition by the Cas12a/crRNA complex triggers trans-cleavage of single-stranded DNA inhibitors, restoring the peroxidase-like activity of MXenes to produce a visible signal. The platform achieved a detection limit of 132 copies/μL……

entry.title: A hierarchical Bayesian approach to estimate the most probable number (MPN) concentration of *Salmonella* in raw chicken from qualitative data

link.title: A hierarchical Bayesian approach to estimate the most probable number (MPN) concentration of *Salmonella* in raw chicken from qualitative data

entry.content:
The Quick Summary

It’s important to know how much Salmonella bacteria might be in chicken to keep our food safe. Scientists made a new way to count Salmonella in chicken using special math, even when they only have simple test results. This new math helps them understand how Salmonella is spread unevenly in food, which is tricky to count.

Original Abstract

Estimating bacterial concentrations in food products is a key element in quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA). A Bayesian probabilistic approach with the most probable number (MPN) technique was developed to estimate the concentration of Salmonella in chicken meat based on the qualitative data. entry.title: Trends and Advances in Development of Photodynamic, Photothermal, and Intelligent Food Packaging: A Review

link.title: Trends and Advances in Development of Photodynamic, Photothermal, and Intelligent Food Packaging: A Review

entry.content:
The Quick Summary

Special food packaging helps keep our food safe and fresh for longer, so less food goes to waste. This paper talks about new types of packaging that use light or heat from light to stop tiny germs and tell us if the food is still good. For example, some packaging uses natural helpers like curcumin that react to light to keep food safe.

Original Abstract

Food packaging has evolved as advanced technologies to reduce food wastage by actively enhancing safety, quality, and sustainability. This review focuses on the mechanisms, materials chemistry, and application performance of photodynamic, photothermal, and intelligent food packaging systems that exploit light-induced chemical and thermal processes for microbial control and freshness monitoring. Photodynamic packaging employs natural photosensitizers, including curcumin, riboflavin, and porphyrin……

entry.title: Use of quantitative indicator microorganism data to determine if turkey re-hang and post-chill sampling are predictive of *Salmonella enterica* contamination in ground turkey

link.title: Use of quantitative indicator microorganism data to determine if turkey re-hang and post-chill sampling are predictive of *Salmonella enterica* contamination in ground turkey

entry.content:
The Quick Summary

Salmonella enterica is a germ often found in turkey that can make people very sick. To stop this, people check turkeys at different steps, like when birds are first hung up or after they’ve been chilled. This study wants to find out if these early checks are a good way to tell if the final ground turkey will have Salmonella enterica and be unsafe.

Original Abstract

Salmonella enterica is a leading cause of foodborne illness worldwide, with poultry products serving as a major source of human infection. In the United States, Salmonella oversight in poultry relies on USDA-FSIS verification testing, which requires sampling 1 out of every 3,000 birds at re-hang and post-chill to assess process control.
